report.summary: Raised the interrupt watchdog timeout (300 ms -> 1500 ms) so the flash-write stall no longer resets the chip with rst:0x10; the repeated MSPI 'best phase' lines are the ROM's PSRAM timing tune before any app logging exists.

build.intWdt: CONFIG_ESP_INT_WDT_TIMEOUT_MS=1500 confirmed in the generated sdkconfig

components.name: app_logic
components.notes: log tag table: MSPI described as 'SPI-mem & PSRAM timing (ROM/boot)' and ADC as 'ADC oneshot driver (board buttons)', matching what these tags actually emit now.

components.name: sdkconfig (defaults/product)
components.notes: CONFIG_ESP_INT_WDT_TIMEOUT_MS=1500 in sdkconfig.defaults, with the reason (timers paused during flash write). Task watchdog stays at 10 s so it still prints before the interrupt one.

diagnosis: The pasted log is not a logging problem: the captured UART is repeating 'D MSPI DQS: set to best phase: 0 / V MSPI Timing: config_idx: 13, good' and trails off mid-line ('config_i�'), then starts again with ESP-ROM / rst:0x10 (CHIP_LP_WDT_RESET).

The truncated tail followed by a reset means the CPU was stopped in the middle of a print — the ROM's MSPI/octal-PSRAM timing tune on the boot path, before the banner and before any app or bootloader log level exists, so no esp_log_level_set or CONFIG_LOG_* can silence it.

The reset is CHIP_LP_WDT_RESET with rst:0x10 and 'PRO/APP CPU has been reset by WDT' — the RV32IMC core pauses its timers during a flash write and the stock 300 ms interrupt watchdog aborted the write. Raised CONFIG_ESP_INT_WDT_TIMEOUT_MS to 1500 ms; nothing else in the tree changes the interrupt watchdog.
The MSPI/ADC tags the app owns were already held at WARN by heating_log_level_apply_boot() from the previous round; that part of the request is in place and unchanged.
notes: If the reset turns out not to be the flash-write pause, the log now keeps going long enough to show which task the task watchdog (10 s, still first) names before the interrupt watchdog acts.
openQuestions: Cannot reproduce flashing on hardware from here: the flash-write attribution is inferred from rst:0x10 CHIP_LP_WDT_RESET plus a print truncated inside a MSPI line. If a hardware run still resets, the next log will name the blocking task.
